perspective:
From Angela Hwang’s available perspective:

- She knows she and Kevin have been close friends since high school and often confide in each other. She knows Kevin works as a construction worker.
- She noticed Kevin seemed unhappy with his construction job and invited him to coffee to talk.
- At coffee, she heard Kevin say he was “alright, just the usual grind”; then that he is not happy, feels stuck and unfulfilled, and is just going through the motions. He said he had thought about changing jobs but did not know where to start and felt overwhelmed. She suggested exploring options together; Kevin agreed and thanked her.
- She felt supportive and hopeful, found job openings and a career-counseling service, and told Kevin about them. He thanked her and said he had thought more about it, was interested in something creative, possibly design or architecture. She encouraged him to check the resources; he said he would and thanked her.
- She believed Kevin was hesitant and felt frustrated and worried. She arranged a meeting with a career coach and told him. Kevin said she didn’t have to, appreciated it, but wasn’t sure he was ready. She encouraged him; he agreed to give it a shot. She promised to support him.
- She believed Kevin was making progress, checked in, and heard him say the coach had been helpful, he had started online design courses, and he felt more confident. She said she was proud and offered more help; Kevin said just knowing she was there was enough.
- She believed Kevin had successfully transitioned to a new career, felt happy and satisfied, and organized a small celebration party. She told him he deserved it. Kevin thanked her and said he couldn’t have done it without her. She said he did the hard work; they celebrated.

Angela has no independent access to Kevin’s private thoughts beyond what he stated, what she observed, and what she inferred from their interactions.
